description: The plot titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-3” illustrates how the sparsity ratio (proportion of values below a 1e-3 threshold) varies across transformer layers for three measurement conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 23 with major tick labels shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 up to about 0.9 with evenly spaced tick labels at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line (legend: “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003”) starts near ~0.015 at layer 0 and stays very close to 0 across all layers, ending near ~0.0 by the final layers; an orange dotted line (legend: “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126”) starts high near ~0.85 at layer 0, drops steeply to around ~0.42 at layer 1 and ~0.16 by about layer 5, then continues decreasing to ~0.02–0.03 by roughly layers 14–18, with small late-layer increases around layers ~19–22 (reaching roughly ~0.07 near layer 21) and ending around ~0.04 at layer 23; a green dash-dot line (legend: “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080”) begins near ~0.80 at layer 0, falls to ~0.28 at layer 1 and ~0.09 by about layer 5, then decreases more gradually to ~0.02 by around layer 10 and approaches ~0.0 (near-baseline values) from approximately layers 14 through 23.
